newsitem.title: USA: Maine governor vetoes cigarette tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Maine governor vetoes cigarette tax increase.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King Monday vetoed a bill to double the state's cigarette tax in a dispute with Democrats over how the new revenue should be used.

"The people of Maine did not send us here to repeat the mistakes of the 1980s, when every available dollar in additional revenue was spent on new or expanded government programs," King said in a statement.

King, who supports the tax increase as an anti-smoking measure, said he would make another attempt when lawmakers met in mid-June, but Democratic leaders quickly downplayed the possibility of a compromise.
The Democrat's bill would have increased the tax to $0.74 per pack and used the revenue to provide health insurance to low income children and prescription drugs for needy senior citizens.

King, an Independent who supports the tax increase in an effort to curb smoking by teenagers, has proposed using most of the money for income tax relief, with a small percentage spent on anti-smoking education efforts.
Democratic leaders said the state had to do more to address the health needs of low-income residents.
"People see a direct connection between smoking and health," Senate President Mark Lawrence said.
Lawmakers are tentatively scheduled to review this and other vetoes on June 19. Neither the House or Senate approved the Democratic-supported bill by veto-proof margins.
